Subjects

Political thought

The state, authority, the caliphate and political movements.

For most of this section the starting point is the end of the caliphate, abolished in 1924. Rashid Rida's The Caliphate or the Supreme Imamate (1922) argued for renewing it. After it went, Hasan al-Banna, Maududi, Sayyid Qutb and Taqi al-Din al-Nabhani each built a programme on what followed. Later authors compare these movements and criticise them (Wael Hallaq, Ovamir Anjum), or ask what the state means for Muslim ethics at all.

Papers from the Yaqeen and Ummatics institutes take up the caliphate and Islamism as present-day questions.

Where to begin

A reading order, earliest first. Each title opens the text or the free copy.

  1. 1922 · Book
    The Caliphate or the Supreme Imamate ↗ Rashīd Riḍā

    Rida's case for a reformed caliphate, written as the Ottoman state was ending.

  2. 1949 · Book
    Social Justice in Islam ↗ Sayyid Quṭb

    Qutb's first major statement of a social programme drawn from Islam.

  3. 1953 · Translation
    The Islamic State ↗ Taqī al-Dīn al-Nabhānī

    The Hizb ut-Tahrir founder's account of the structure of an Islamic state.

  4. 1964 · Book
    Milestones ↗ Sayyid Quṭb

    Qutb's call for a vanguard, one of the most discussed Islamist texts of the century.

  5. 2013 · Book
    The Impossible State: Islam, Politics, and Modernity's Moral Predicament Wael Hallaq

    Hallaq's argument that the modern state is a poor fit for Islamic governance.

  6. 2019 · Paper
    Who Wants the Caliphate? ↗ Ovamir Anjum

    Ovamir Anjum on what Muslims mean when they speak of a caliphate.
